subject: Performance SLOs: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Hi Samir / Ellie —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can qualify the performance SLOs and scope a short PoC: 

What we heard from you:
- Target end-to-end (client->Redwood->model->client) p95: 450ms, p99: 900ms for the synchronous generation path (single-turn requests, average 100 tokens).
- Current provider observed p95 ~700ms, p99 ~1.6s for the same traffic profile; streaming disabled for most calls today.
- Production throughput target: 120 QPS sustained, burst to 300 QPS during peak; concurrency (parallel outstanding requests) ~ 250.
- Streaming requirement: for chat/assistant flows you want server-sent streaming with first-byte latency under 300ms and consistent chunk cadence for UX.

Redwood follow-ups / proposed test plan:
1) We will run an end-to-end hosted API benchmark against a Redwood-verified model with your representative prompt set and token lengths (we'll use the sample set you shared).
2) We'll replicate your concurrency/throughput profile (120 QPS sustained, 300 QPS burst) and capture p50/p95/p99 and first-byte streaming latency.
3) Share raw latency logs + summary CSV and an initial SLO proposal (p95/p99 targets + recommended fallbacks).
4) If numbers look good, schedule a 2-week dedicated PoC on our Dedicated pool or private deployment based on your preference.

Can you confirm the representative prompt set and attach a 30-minute window of production logs (anonymized) that show the current provider's latency histogram? That will help us mirror the workload.

I've attached the call recording and a short latency snapshot you sent during the call (please confirm it's the right one). We'll push a formal SLO proposal by EOD Friday after the first bench run.

Thanks —
Laura
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: call-recording-0225.mp4, finlytics-latency-snapshot-0225.csv

From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellie Zhao <ellie.zhao@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Laura —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the targets are correct. A few clarifications: 
- The 700ms/1.6s numbers are aggregated across our CDN + model endpoint; the host-side (model inference only) p95 is closer to 300ms on our current provider. So network/cold-starts and our serialization layer are contributing a lot.
- For streaming UX, first-byte under 300ms is ideal but acceptable up to 450ms; our frontend expects steady chunks every 150-300ms once streaming starts.
- We can share a 30-min anonymized log. Attaching the primary latency CSV from yesterday (same file you attached back).

Question: can you simulate our serialization overhead? We do a small per-request JSON envelope and TLS termination in our edgenode — if Redwood can point to a recommended setup (or we give you the exact encoding/headers) that would help the benchmark be realistic.

Samir
Head of Infrastructure, FinLytics
samir@finlytics.com

Attachment: finlytics-latency-snapshot-0225.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>, Ellie Zhao <ellie.zhao@finlytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Thanks Samir — good context. Quick notes from Redwood infra/bench perspective and next steps so we can scope the PoC: 

What we'll run for the initial hosted bench (this week):
- Test profile: 100-token avg responses, mix of 70% single-turn generation + 30% streaming chat.
- Concurrency/throughput: ramp to 120 QPS sustained (over 15m window), simulate bursts up to 300 QPS for 2m, test up to 250 parallel outstanding requests.
- Network/serialization: Aditya will model your JSON envelope + TLS overhead if you share the exact payload size and typical headers.
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 end-to-end, first-byte streaming latency, token-throughput, error rates, and tail latencies under burst.

Deliverables: 
- Raw CSV + summary dashboard link
- SLO proposal doc (p95/p99 targets, recommended fallbacks/variant routing)
- Quick checklist for production readiness if you move to Dedicated/Private (KV cache, batching config, quantization notes).

Aditya — can you confirm you can model Samir's serialization and run a bench on our hosted cluster by EOD Thursday? Samir/ Ellie — if you can drop the exact request payload example (including headers) into the Drive link, we'll pick it up.

Thanks —
Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Feb 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: p95/p99 end-to-end latency (hosted vs current provider)

Marissa/Aditya —

Appreciate the plan. Uploaded a small sample payload and anonymized logs to the Drive link you included. A couple of items to confirm: 
- Our typical request payload (JSON + headers) is ~1.8 KB compressed, average output 100 tokens (~600 bytes).
- We currently terminate TLS at our edge (nginx), so if your bench sends requests directly to Redwood hosted endpoints we should add a 6-8ms per-request TLS overhead to match reality. Feel free to add a synthetic 8ms per request in the bench config.
- For the PoC, we prefer starting on Hosted to validate latency profile end-to-end and then discuss Dedicated for steady-state throughput/cost optimization.

Proposed immediate next step: run your hosted bench with the payload + 8ms synthetic TLS and share results next business day. If the p95/p99 meet our targets, we'll scope a 2-week PoC.

Samir
